# Scientific computation specification

**Note:** This file was generated by ChatGPT 5.6 Sol under the direction of Adam Phillippy.

This file is normative. Historical alternatives and benchmark narratives belong in
architecture decision records, not in the current scientific contract.

## Input and coordinates

Core coordinates are zero-based and half-open. The UI alone converts them to one-based
inclusive labels. Sequence positions are never removed during normalization.

A FASTA header is split at its first whitespace. The first field is the sequence
identifier used by scientific objects and numeric outputs; the trimmed remainder is
presentation-only description text. Source filenames and load-order suffixes may
disambiguate selectors and output filenames but never change the biological sequence
identifier or numeric result.

| Input | Packed behavior | K-mer behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `A C G T` in either case | Valid DNA base | Included |
| `U` or `u` | Normalized to `T` | Identical to `T` at the same coordinate |
| IUPAC ambiguity (`R Y S W K M B D H V N`) | Coordinate retained, invalid bit set | Every overlapping k-mer is omitted |
| Gap (`-` or `.`) | Coordinate retained, invalid bit set | Every overlapping k-mer is omitted |
| FASTA whitespace and line endings | Syntax only, no coordinate | Ignored |
| FASTA line beginning `;` | Comment, no coordinate | Ignored |
| Any other non-whitespace symbol | Input error | Parsing stops |

A selected pair uses the longer record length as a square common domain. Cells beyond
the end of the shorter record are missing, not zero-similarity. At most one billion
bases are accepted per record. This is an input bound, not yet a claim that every
browser can process a 1 Gb record within available memory.

## Canonical k-mers and hashing

`k` must be in `1..=31`; the interface defaults to 21. Forward and reverse-complement
k-mers are represented as two-bit words and the lexicographically smaller word is
canonical. Palindromes have `Both` orientation.

Production uses the canonical ntHash2 split-rotation recurrence. Published constants
and vectors are pinned to ntHash source commit
`c26bd4572a19de81e30d55042dbd33c1fd21d4b6`. No alternate production hash is compiled.
Production seed zero is the exact published stream. Offline multi-seed validation may
apply `fmix64(ntHash2 ^ seed)` to sample independent OPH layouts; this seeded permutation
is not exposed by the browser. The finalizer also decorrelates HLL input internally.

## Axis intervals

For resolution `r`, k-mer start coordinates are assigned exactly to `2r` half-bin
segments. A core cell is the union of its two half bins. Its expanded target is the
union of the core and one neighboring half bin on each side, clipped to the sequence.
This is the ModDotPlot half-window expansion that reduces grid-registration artifacts.
Each k-mer hash is streamed once into the applicable half-bin summary; no
chromosome-wide k-mer/hash array is retained.

## OPH representation

Each summary contains an undensified one-permutation sketch. The top `log2(m)` hash
bits select one of `m` registers; the smallest full hash in the register wins. Empty
registers remain empty. Winner orientation is combined if the same canonical k-mer is
observed on both source strands.

The production matrix representation is `FrozenAxis`: occupancy, 32 winner fingerprint
bit planes, orientation bit planes, observation/cardinality scalars, and coordinate
bounds. Ordinary browser axes do not retain complete k-mer sets. Mutable full-winner
builders are discarded after freezing. A test-only scalar comparator checks the
optimized word-parallel counters. Non-default validation builds may additionally retain
bounded exact sets for controlled experiments; those sets are outside the production
contract.

For two aligned signatures:

```text
U = registers occupied in at least one signature
M = registers whose occupied 32-bit winner fingerprints agree
J_hat = M / U
```

This is the OPH matched-winner estimator `Nmat / (k - Nemp)`. The 14 low-bit planes
remain an execution prefilter and provenance field, but the scientific Jaccard estimate
uses verified winners. Validation found no 32-bit false winner matches in the tested
multi-seed matrix sweep; the risk is tracked matrix-wide rather than treated as zero.

HLL precision 10 estimates distinct cardinalities `|A|` and `|B|`. With estimated
Jaccard `J`, intersection and directed containment are:

```text
I_hat = J * (|A| + |B|) / (1 + J)
C_hat(A in B) = clamp(I_hat / |A|, 0, 1)
```

## Displayed score

For core intervals `X` and `Y`, and half-window expansions `X+` and `Y+`:

```text
C_x = containment(X, Y+)
C_y = containment(Y, X+)
C   = max(C_x, C_y)
ANI_c = C^(1/k)
```

`ANI_c` is the historical ModDotPlot label for the containment-derived display
transform. It is not biological average nucleotide identity and is not asserted to be
equivalent to an alignment-derived measure such as `ANI_m`. The scientific acceptance
target is estimated containment versus exact containment of complete canonical k-mer
sets. `ANI_c` comparisons validate only the transformed, quantized product output.

The maximum containment controls the display score, while direction evidence from both
directed comparisons is pooled. The score is stored as `round(ANI_c * 10000)` in
`u16`; `65535` means missing. A self cell on the principal diagonal is exactly 10000 by
invariant.

Direction votes are forward when matching canonical winners have equal unambiguous
source orientations and reverse when they differ. `Both`/unknown observations are
ambiguous. The numeric direction is `(forward - reverse)/(forward + reverse)`. The
renderer preserves its sign and identity luminance but reduces chroma at low support;
visual confidence therefore does not alter the scientific match value.

## Quality tiers and operating domain

The default preview uses 256 registers and is explicitly provisional. The default
detailed tier uses 1,024 registers and HLL precision 10. Detailed tiles are requested
only when the preview has low winner support or lies near a display decision. Preview
tiles remain the settled result elsewhere. Navigation cancels obsolete work. Sparse
correction is not part of the browser protocol or ordinary web build.

Under independent point substitutions, with large indels excluded, k-mer survival at
unaltered-base fraction `q` is approximately `q^k`. This is the only biological
quantity against which `ANI_c` is intended to be compared, following Figure 4 of the
ModDotPlot paper. At `k=21`, `q=0.80` retains only about 0.92% of exact k-mers, so
containment evidence becomes sparse in this regime.
The default display uses the reversed 11-class ColorBrewer Spectral palette on a white
plot background: lower displayed identity begins at the purple end and higher identity
reaches the red end. The background is shown below 85%; the 80% control is retained for
advanced inspection, not as a promise of uniform sensitivity. Palette direction and
individual display colors affect presentation only, not numeric tiles or estimator
semantics.

The non-default Rust `validation` feature preserves the rejected sparse-correction
experiment solely for controlled estimator comparisons. It may retain a complete
canonical-hash set while a core has at most 2,048 distinct hashes and rescan eligible
directed containment when the historical match-detection model falls below 99% at an
80% floor. These routines are not part of the browser protocol, Wasm surface, ordinary
web build, production estimator, or release accuracy contract. The historical policy
and its limitations are recorded in ADR 0004.

## Terminal exact mode

When the view reaches one matrix position per base, sketches stop. Equal valid
canonical k-mers match exactly. The exact renderer paints each
match across its complete k-base alignment: equal canonical orientations paint a
forward diagonal and opposite orientations paint the corresponding reverse diagonal.

For even-k reverse-complement-palindromic k-mers, canonical orientation is ambiguous.
The footprint represents both possible diagonals with neutral direction evidence.
Unequal valid k-mer starts mismatch. Ambiguity-overlapping and padded starts are
missing unless another valid exact match covers the position. Missing evidence remains
numerically distinct from identity zero and uses a separate display shade. Initial
views already at terminal resolution enter this mode before drawing their first tile.

Exact similarity coloring is independently selectable. **Bases** is the default and
colors a matched cell by the corresponding base from the X sequence; **Identity** uses the configured similarity
palette. The exact visualization mode and fixed full-footprint geometry are recorded
in display provenance. Visualization changes redraw cached textures without changing
the exact numeric tile.

## Configuration and change control

Every production sketch tile is governed by an immutable `ScientificConfig` containing
schema version, `k`, hash identity/seed field, register count,
comparison/verification widths, OPH estimator, HLL precision, expansion and ANI
transforms, fixed-point scale, and missing sentinel. Sparse-correction fields are fixed
to their disabled values in production. Non-default validation configurations may
populate those fields for controlled experiments. Validation occurs before allocation.
A stable digest is part of worker messages, renderer cache keys, UI provenance, and
numeric/image exports.

Any change to numeric output requires a configuration-version decision, exact-oracle
comparison, optimized/scalar equivalence where applicable, spatial and threshold
metrics, and updated release evidence.

The complete claim boundary, test tiers, and post-v0.2.0 gates are frozen in
[VALIDATION_CONTRACT.md](VALIDATION_CONTRACT.md).
